_note: The gesture book (pepin.expression.book): the motion atoms, the compositions the brain names in its text ({laugh}) or through the gesture tool, the arm poses taught by hand, the idle layer and the robot's moments. An atom is ONE cycle of keys at shares (at 0..1) of its period_s; a value is a number, "$param" or "-$param" of its params (drawn uniformly from [lo, hi] at each performance); repeats and hold_s are reserved. Degrees: the head's pan_deg + left, tilt_deg + down (offsets on whatever holds the head); the arm's joints in config/arm.json's convention (additive: offsets on the pose under it; absolute: a pose, starting and ending on rest); the wheels' yaw_deg + left and x_m + forward (pepin.expression.wheels; sized to config/expression.json's wheels caps at speed 1, a clip faster than them is refused). A step's at_s puts the atom's stroke (stroke x its first cycle) that far from the marker's word (negative: before it), p is the chance it plays, params narrow the atom's ranges, a string or a list of strings names a face (name) or a pose (pose). Timing and variety from .claude/research/brain/expression/expressive_motion.md (2026-10-11): strokes on the word or up to 0.2 s before it, amplitude ranges of about +-20 %, period ranges of about +-12 %, optional parts with their odds, mirror images, never the same variant twice running. Arm atoms are sized to keep config/arm.json's caps (90 deg/s, 360 deg/s^2) at speed 1: the arm's beats and clicks are slow, so emphasis and laughter ride the head and the face; raise the caps on the bench before raising these.

poses.note: Arm poses, one angle per joint of config/arm.json, and a note each: TAUGHT by hand (scripts/gesture.py teach NAME: torque off, the arm placed, its six angles written here) or AUTHORED from the URDF (pepin.arm's forward kinematics of the vendored URDF on config/arm.json's mount, the link boxes ungrown against config/body.json's cart and mast, the speaker box, the pan servo and an estimated head box swept over the neck's whole reach; scratch/arm_poses_1012/). rest is not here: it is config/arm.json's motion.rest_deg. A step naming a pose that is not here is left out (the rest of the gesture plays). A step that names a pose sets period_s so the move from rest keeps the caps: the largest joint travel d moves at 1.5 d / period_s at its fastest (90 deg/s: period_s >= d / 60).

raised.note: TAUGHT by hand 2026-10-12: the forearm forward, the hand up, ready to wave; from the URDF: the hand 8.7 cm from the body and from the head's whole reach, the upper arm 3.2 cm from the speaker box; the hand in the level view; 112 deg from rest, 1.86 s at the caps

ready.note: AUTHORED from the URDF 2026-10-12: half raised, the elbow bent, the hand level and forward toward a person ahead on the centre line; the hand 8.1 cm from the body and 9.4 cm from the head's whole reach, the upper arm 3.1 cm from the speaker box; below the level view; 57 deg from rest, 0.98 s at the caps

offer.note: AUTHORED from the URDF 2026-10-12: the open hand forward and low toward the person, the moving jaw up (wrist_roll 0: the fixed jaw a palm under it); the hand 6.5 cm from the body and 9.3 cm from the head's whole reach, the upper arm 2.9 cm from the speaker box; below the level view; 69 deg from rest, 1.14 s at the caps

emphasis.note: AUTHORED from the URDF 2026-10-12: the forearm up beside the head on the right, the hand up and shut (a raised fist for a beat); the hand 3.9 cm from the head's whole reach (7.9 cm in the conversation band), the elbow 4.7 cm from the mast; beside the view; 100 deg from rest, 1.67 s at the caps

thinking.note: AUTHORED from the URDF 2026-10-12: the hand raised to the chin's height in front and to the right of the head, the elbow back; the hand 3.9 cm from the head's whole reach (6.1 cm in the conversation band), the upper arm 3.0 cm from the speaker box; 1 % of the arm in the level view's lower corner; 88 deg from rest, 1.47 s at the caps

tucked.note: AUTHORED from the URDF 2026-10-12: close to the body, the forearm upright beside the mast and the hand bent in toward the face (shy, sorry); the hand 3.9 cm from the head's whole reach (4.3 cm in the conversation band), the upper arm 2.5 cm from the speaker box; out of the view; 98 deg from rest, 1.64 s at the caps

head_nod.note: down and back up, at most 2.5 Hz: the gaze arbiter refuses a tilt that turns back sooner than 0.2 s (clip_max_hz 2.5; the mast rings at 5.3 Hz), and the tilt's 600 deg/s^2 ramp needs 0.2 s for a 6 deg stroke (4 d / T^2), so a 0.4 s cycle at 6 deg is both limits at once; no counter-lift before the stroke: a 1 deg lift in 0.06 s is a turn the arbiter refuses whatever its size

head_shake.note: no: either side first; the pan's first quarter cycle needs 4 d / T^2 within its 2232 deg/s^2 ramp (config/neck.json): 8 deg in 0.125 s

head_back.note: the head up and held (energy, joy, a laugh's throw back)

head_drop.note: the head down and held (sadness, doubt, sympathy)

head_glance.note: a look away, up and to a side, and back (thinking: seen as thoughtful and interrupted less)

head_cock.note: the stand-in for a head tilt (the neck has no roll)

recoil.note: a quick lift of the head (surprise), held, settled slowly; as quick as the tilt's 600 deg/s^2 ramp allows: 8 deg in 0.25 s

head_drift.note: the idle layer's fidget: a small slow look aside and back

breath.note: +-0.6 deg at 0.25 Hz (config/face.json's breathe_hz), a looped overlay (loop: the arbiter repeats it until released or lapsed); within the arbiter's clip_still_deg (1 deg) it never blinds the head; not in the idle list below

body_turn.note: a turn in place (stays turned); 30 deg in 1.5 s keeps config/expression.json's wheels caps (30 deg/s, 90 deg/s^2) at speed 1

body_wiggle.note: a slow sway, yaw +-2-4 deg, back to the start pose; the wheels' ramp (90 deg/s^2) makes anything quicker than ~1.8 s a cycle a refusal

body_rock.note: forward 1-2 cm and back; 2 cm each way in 0.45 s keeps the wheels' ramp (0.5 m/s^2) at speed 1

arm_pose.note: rest -> a pose of poses in period_s (the stroke: arriving; the default 1.3 s keeps a move of up to 78 deg within 90 deg/s and 360 deg/s^2, a step naming a pose further from rest sets its own period_s), held hold_s; then the board takes the arm back to rest by itself at its caps and lets go

arm_wave.note: the hand waved forward and back by the wrist on the pose under it (raised when taught, else rest): the bye wave; +-9 deg at ~1.7 Hz is the most the servos' 2232 deg/s^2 allows (peak acceleration ~75 amp / period^2)

arm_wave_side.note: the hand waved side to side by the shoulder's pan on the pose under it: the hello wave (the wrist wave reads as bye); +-9 deg at ~1.7 Hz is the most the servos' 2232 deg/s^2 allows (peak acceleration ~75 amp / period^2)

arm_beat.note: a down-stroke of the wrist and its rebound; a beat wants 0.15-0.25 s, the caps give 0.45 s (timid until raised)

arm_flourish.note: the hand opened outward by the wrist alone (a shrug's open palm); the shoulder only moves through taught poses

wrist_turn.note: so-so: the wrist rolled one way and the other

gripper_click.note: open and shut (the stroke: shut), a quick clack at ~1.8 Hz: 5-7 deg is what the servos' 2232 deg/s^2 allows at that tempo

gripper_set.note: the gripper opened by amp_deg, held, shut

face.note: one of config/face.json's expressions (name), held hold_s, then the face lapses to what stood before

greeting.note: hello: a happy face a little before the word, the head up, the hand raised and waved side to side, the wave starting on the way up; long: it may run 1 s past the speech; the floor: the face and a nod

farewell.note: bye: a smile, the hand raised and waved forward and back starting on the way up, or a nod; the head dropped a little after; long: it may run 1 s past the speech; the floor: the smile and a nod

laugh.note: the face first, the head thrown back on the word, then a bob of the head (or a wiggle of the body); the gripper chatters now and then; the floor: the grin and the head thrown back

doubt.note: hmm: a skewed mouth, the hand half raised and the wrist so-so, the head cocked (or down a little and aside); at most 2 s of arm: the raise 0.8-0.9 s, held 0.3-0.5 s, one so-so of the wrist on the word; the floor: the mouth and the cocked head

thinking.note: a look away up and to a side, the thinking mouth, now and then the hand to the chin after the look has begun (also the slow tool's moment: it fills the wait); at most 2 s of arm: the hand up in 0.9-1.1 s, held 0.4-0.6 s; the floor: the look and the mouth

emphasis.note: a single sudden nod on the stressed word; now and then a beat of the raised fist (slow at the first caps); bound to its word (never late); the floor: the nod

surprise.note: an O mouth just before, the head lifted on the word, the arm half raised now and then, a slow settle; at most 2 s of arm: the raise 0.9-1.1 s, held 0.3-0.6 s; the floor: the mouth and the lift

agreement.note: yes: a nod or two, a smile now and then, the open hand offered now and then; at most 2 s of arm: the offer in 0.9-1.1 s, held 0.3-0.6 s; the floor: a nod and a smile

disagreement.note: no: a shake or two, a flat mouth, now and then the hand half raised and the wrist so-so; at most 2 s of arm: the raise 0.8-0.9 s, held 0.3-0.5 s, one so-so of the wrist; the floor: the shake and the mouth

shrug.note: who knows: the open hand offered and turned out, the head down a little and aside, a flat or thinking mouth; at most 2 s of arm: the offer in 0.8-0.9 s, held 0.3-0.5 s, the hand turned out in 0.9-1.0 s on the word; the floor: the head down and the mouth

evil_click.note: the mischievous one (world domination): the hand raised, the gripper clacking quickly on the way up and at the top, a clenched grin, the head lowered; marker only, once in five minutes; the floor: the grin and the head lowered

sympathy.note: small and slow: the head down (or cocked), a worried mouth, now and then the hand drawn in to the face (tucked); at most 2 s of arm: drawn in over 0.9-1.1 s, held 0.4-0.6 s; the floor: the head down and the mouth

moments.note: a moment of the robot (pepin.expression.conversation) -> the composition it performs, under the caps; greeting_due and farewell_due: the person's hello and bye, played in the brain's wait by the engine's listeners
